correctness.rationale: Every deficient vertex has degree below \(k\) and is forced into any seed set. In the nontrivial case \(d<k\), a minimum set has exactly \(k\) seeds. Before an incomplete part \(i\) activates, one of its unseeded vertices sees exactly \(k-s_i+U\) active neighbours, where \(U\) is the accumulated number of newly activated vertices outside that part; hence activation is exactly \(U\ge s_i\). Sorting incomplete parts by \(s_i\) turns the dynamics into the stated greedy parking recurrence, proving necessity and sufficiency. The binomial count then follows independently within parts. The bundled exhaustive program checks the literal dynamics through order eight but is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Minimum cardinality alone leaves a genuine intervention-design ambiguity because optimum-size placements can fail. The theorem resolves that ambiguity completely on a canonical dense family, supplies a fast membership test and counts all optimal placements exactly.
residual_risks: Older literature may use weakly indexed aliases such as perfect target set, dynamic monopoly or contagious set.

final_claim: For a complete multipartite graph under a uniform irreversible \(k\)-threshold process, every minimum conversion set is characterized exactly by the deficient-part condition and a sorted weighted-parking inequality on the incomplete nondeficient parts; the theorem also gives the exact binomial profile count of all minimum sets.
limitations: Uniform thresholds and complete multipartite graphs only.
The theorem classifies minimum conversion sets, not all nonminimum conversion sets.
